# Using The Repository Harness
<!-- doc-role:overview -->

<!-- Generated by repo-harness-builder; source: core/docs:3.0 -->

Use the three generated skills as a loop: recover context, keep durable documentation current, then leave a verified handoff.

## Daily Workflow
<!-- doc-role:daily-workflow -->

1. Start or resume with `repo-harness-session-start` and state the objective. It reports a scoped outcome, reconciles context with repository evidence, inspects Git read-only, and ends with one concrete remote-check question when safe.
2. Use `repo-harness-documentation` when durable documentation or visible project state needs updating.
3. Pause or close with `repo-harness-session-stop`. It completes documentation and Engram continuity first, screens each changed path, then may request one outcome-scoped approval for an exact commit, push, or combined commit and push.

## Integrated Availability
<!-- doc-role:availability -->

Confirm the generated skills are available in the selected runtime and that Gentle AI and Engram are available. If either continuity dependency is unavailable, report it and do not claim integrated continuity.

## Congruence And Ownership
<!-- doc-role:ownership -->

Run `python .repo-harness/check.py` after canonical skills or runtime projections change. Root `.gitattributes` preserves LF checkout bytes through exact `.repo-harness/check.py text eol=lf` and `.repo-harness/manifest.json text eol=lf` rules. The checker proves on-disk parity, not whether the active process refreshed its registered skill content. Same-process older registered content is an expected cache limitation; defer that optional validation to a fresh process or a supported explicit registry reload without inventing a command. Engram carries temporary cross-session context; repository files remain authoritative.

## Approval Boundaries
<!-- doc-role:approval-boundaries -->

The daily skills inspect read-only by default. Outcomes are `ready`, `paused`, `blocked`, `failed`, `completed`, or `degraded`, and `paused` means human input is actually needed. Explicit safe-sync consent covers bounded fetch plus fast-forward-only integration. Explicit combined commit-and-push consent covers exact staging, commit, checks, one fetch preflight, and one push to the identified upstream. Commit-only and push-only remain narrow. Changed scope, sensitive or unrelated files, divergence, destination or credential changes, destructive integration, hook mutation, or verification failure invalidates consent.

Builder apply is separate and strict: English uses exact `APPROVE` or `DENY`; Spanish uses exact `APROBAR` or `DENEGAR`. The CLI receives the resolved language explicitly and requires both the current plan digest and exact active-domain approval. Direct CLI calls default to English. Generated daily session skills remain conversational.
